title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative: With the growing informalization of work, Trade Union organizations in South Africa are having to institute new and innovative approaches to reach out to and mobilize different groups of workers, including those not in standard employment relationships; and to promote advocacy for the extension of collective bargaining agreements to workers in vulnerable sectors of the economy. International Labour Standards (ILS) is a growing area interest for the workers with an expressed need to enhance their institutional capacities to play an active role in the application of ILS and to advocate for the ratification of Conventions which address their conditions of work; as well as to promote inclusivity, and decent work for workers under situations of vulnerability. The Workers have decried the lack of effective collective bargaining particularly in the public sector where collective bargaining agreements are not upheld and where capacity challenges to engage effectively in collective bargaining processes persist for their members. As actors for change, the workers’ organizations in Eswatini are not optimally engaged in influencing economic, social, and environmental policies through the UN Cooperation Framework processes. The strategy will focus on capacity building support to strengthen workers organizations on ILS and to apply ratified ILS; support to workers’ advocacy for the ratification of up-to-date Conventions including C183 and C151; capacity support to workers’ organizational capacities to mainstream gender, promote gender equity, mitigate against violence and harassment in the world of work; to promote the protection of the rights of workers in situations of vulnerability; and to strengthen workers’ effective engagement in collective bargaining .
